title: Trigonometric Functions: Radians, Values, Signs and Sum Formulas
seo_title: Trigonometric Functions Class 11 Worksheet with Answers (NCERT Chapter 3)
standard_text: Positive and negative angles; measuring angles in radians and in degrees and conversion from one measure to another; definition of trigonometric functions with the help of the unit circle; truth of the identity sin²x + cos²x = 1 for all x; signs of trigonometric functions; domain and range of trigonometric functions and their graphs; expressing sin(x ± y) and cos(x ± y) in terms of sin x, sin y, cos x and cos y; identities related to sin 2x, cos 2x, tan 2x, sin 3x, cos 3x and tan 3x (summary of the CBSE syllabus)
meta_desc: Class 11 Trigonometric Functions worksheet (NCERT Chapter 3): radians and degrees, arc length, values in all four quadrants, sum and difference formulas, multiple angles, period and range. 100 questions with answers.
key_big: π radian = 180°; l = rθ with θ in radians.
key_sub: All, Sin, Tan, Cos: the functions that are positive in quadrants I, II, III, IV.
body_html:
How it works

  • π radian = 180°, so 1° = π/180 radian. To change degrees to radians multiply by π/180.
  • Arc length: l = rθ, with θ in radians.
  • Signs: all positive in the first quadrant, only sin (and cosec) in the second, tan (and cot) in the third, cos (and sec) in the fourth.
  • Large angles: take away whole turns of 360°, then use the reference angle and the sign of the quadrant.
  • sin(x + y) = sin x cos y + cos x sin y; cos(x + y) = cos x cos y − sin x sin y; sin 2x = 2 sin x cos x; cos 2x = cos²x − sin²x.
Example

Find sin 765°.

765° − 2 × 360° = 45°

sin 45° = 1/√2

Answer: 1/√2

Example

Convert 40°20′ to radians.

40°20′ = 121/3 degrees

× π/180 = 121π/540

Answer: 121π/540

Common mistakes

  • Using θ in degrees in l = rθ.
  • Forgetting the sign of the quadrant.
  • Writing sin(A + B) = sin A + sin B.

items.q: The minute hand of a clock is 14 cm long. How far does its tip move in 30 minutes (π = 22/7)?
items.e: In 30 minutes the hand turns 30 × 6° = 180° = π radian. Distance = rθ = 44 cm.

items.q: An arc of length 443 cm subtends an angle of 60° at the centre. Find the radius (π = 22/7).
items.e: 60° = π/3 radian, and r = l ÷ θ = 14 cm.

items.q: An arc of length 40 cm subtends an angle θ at the centre of a circle of radius 5 cm. Find θ in radians.
items.e: θ = l ÷ r = 40 ÷ 5 = 8 radians.

items.q: Convert π3 radians to degrees.
items.e: Multiply by 180/π (replace π with 180°): 60°.

items.q: Find the value of sin(−60°).
items.e: −60° and 300° end in the same place (whole turns of 360° do not matter). That is in the fourth quadrant, with reference angle 60°, where sin is negative. So sin(−60°) = −√3/2.

items.q: Which point is on the unit circle at an angle of 210°?
c: (√32, −12)
(−√32, −12)
(−12, −√32)
(−√32, 12)
items.e: The point is (cos θ, sin θ). The reference angle gives the sizes and the quadrant gives the signs. (−√32, −12).

items.q: sin θ is positive and cos θ is positive. In which quadrant is the terminal side of θ?
items.e: sin is the y-coordinate and cos is the x-coordinate. y positive and x positive gives the first quadrant.

items.q: If sin θ = 45 and θ is in the first quadrant, what is cos θ?
items.e: Use a right triangle with sides 3, 4 and 5. In the first quadrant, x is positive and y is positive, so x = 3, y = 4, r = 5. cos θ = 35.

items.q: If tan θ = 23 and θ is in the first quadrant, find sec² θ.
items.e: sec² θ = 1 + tan² θ = 1 + 49 = 139.

items.q: If sin θ = −1517 and θ is in the fourth quadrant, what is csc θ?
items.e: Use a right triangle with sides 8, 15 and 17. In the fourth quadrant, x is positive and y is negative, so x = 8, y = −15, r = 17. csc θ = −1715.

items.q: Find the exact value of sec 2π3.
items.e: sec = 1 ÷ cos. cos 2π3 = −12, so sec 2π3 = −2.

items.q: Find the exact value of csc 11π6.
items.e: csc = 1 ÷ sin. sin 11π6 = −12, so csc 11π6 = −2.

items.q: If sin θ = −2129 and θ is in the third quadrant, what is cot θ?
items.e: Use a right triangle with sides 20, 21 and 29. In the third quadrant, x is negative and y is negative, so x = −20, y = −21, r = 29. cot θ = 2021.

items.q: If sin θ = 27, find cos² θ.
items.e: cos² θ = 1 − sin² θ = 1 − 449 = 4549. Squares do not depend on the quadrant.

items.q: Find the exact value of csc 7π6.
items.e: csc = 1 ÷ sin. sin 7π6 = −12, so csc 7π6 = −2.

items.q: If tan θ = 34 and θ is in the first quadrant, find sec² θ.
items.e: sec² θ = 1 + tan² θ = 1 + 916 = 2516.

items.q: If cos θ = 1213 and θ is in the first quadrant, what is csc θ?
items.e: Use a right triangle with sides 12, 5 and 13. In the first quadrant, x is positive and y is positive, so x = 12, y = 5, r = 13. csc θ = 135.

items.q: If cot θ = 3, find csc² θ.
items.e: csc² θ = 1 + cot² θ = 1 + 9 = 10.

items.q: Find the exact value of sec 5π3.
items.e: sec = 1 ÷ cos. cos 5π3 = 12, so sec 5π3 = 2.

items.q: If cos θ = −2425 and θ is in the second quadrant, what is sin θ?
items.e: Use a right triangle with sides 24, 7 and 25. In the second quadrant, x is negative and y is positive, so x = −24, y = 7, r = 25. sin θ = 725.

items.q: If cos θ = 725 and θ is in the first quadrant, what is tan θ?

items.q: Find the exact value of sec 3π4.

items.q: If cos θ = 513 and θ is in the fourth quadrant, what is cot θ?
items.e: Use a right triangle with sides 5, 12 and 13. In the fourth quadrant, x is positive and y is negative, so x = 5, y = −12, r = 13. cot θ = −512.

items.q: If sin θ = 25, find csc² θ.
items.e: csc² θ = 1 / sin² θ = 1 ÷ 425 = 254. Squares do not depend on the quadrant.

items.q: If cot θ = 512, find csc² θ.
items.e: csc² θ = 1 + cot² θ = 1 + 25144 = 169144.

items.q: Find the exact value of cos 345°.
items.e: Write 345° = 300° + 45° and use cos(A + B) = cos A cos B − sin A sin B. The result simplifies to √6 + √24.

items.q: Find the exact value of cos 195°.
items.e: Write 195° = 150° + 45° and use cos(A + B) = cos A cos B − sin A sin B. The result simplifies to −√6 + √24.

items.q: α and β are in the first quadrant with sin α = 1517 and cos β = 817. Find cos(α − β).
items.e: cos α = 817 and sin β = 1517 (from right triangles). cos(α − β) = cos α cos β + sin α sin β = 1.

items.q: α and β are in the first quadrant with sin α = 45 and cos β = 725. Find sin(α − β).
items.e: cos α = 35 and sin β = 2425 (from right triangles). sin(α − β) = sin α cos β − cos α sin β = −44125.

items.q: α and β are in the first quadrant with sin α = 45 and cos β = 513. Find sin(α − β).
items.e: cos α = 35 and sin β = 1213 (from right triangles). sin(α − β) = sin α cos β − cos α sin β = −1665.

items.q: α and β are in the first quadrant with sin α = 1213 and cos β = 513. Find cos(α − β).
items.e: cos α = 513 and sin β = 1213 (from right triangles). cos(α − β) = cos α cos β + sin α sin β = 1.

items.q: α and β are in the first quadrant with sin α = 45 and cos β = 35. Find cos(α − β).
items.e: cos α = 35 and sin β = 45 (from right triangles). cos(α − β) = cos α cos β + sin α sin β = 1.

items.q: Find the exact value of tan 75°.
items.e: Write 75° = 45° + 30° and use tan(A + B) = (tan A + tan B) / (1 − tan A tan B). The result simplifies to 2 + √3.

items.q: α and β are in the first quadrant with sin α = 1517 and cos β = 725. Find cos(α − β).
items.e: cos α = 817 and sin β = 2425 (from right triangles). cos(α − β) = cos α cos β + sin α sin β = 416425.

items.q: If sin θ = 725 and θ is in the first quadrant, find cos 2θ.
items.e: First, cos θ = 2425 (sign from the first quadrant). cos 2θ = cos² θ − sin² θ = 576625 − 49625 = 527625.

items.q: What is the range of f(x) = 2 cos x + 1?
items.e: cos x lies between −1 and 1, so 2 cos x lies between −2 and 2: the range is [−1, 3].

items.q: What is the range of f(x) = 5 cos x − 2?
items.e: cos x lies between −1 and 1, so 5 cos x lies between −5 and 5: the range is [−7, 3].

items.q: If cos θ = 45 and θ is in the fourth quadrant, find tan 2θ.
items.e: First, sin θ = −35 (sign from the fourth quadrant). tan 2θ = sin 2θ / cos 2θ = −2425 ÷ 725 = −247.

items.q: What is the period of f(x) = 2sin 4x?
items.e: sin has period 2π, so sin 4x has period 2π ÷ 4 = π/2.

items.q: If sin θ = 817 and θ is in the second quadrant, find cos 2θ.
items.e: First, cos θ = −1517 (sign from the second quadrant). cos 2θ = cos² θ − sin² θ = 225289 − 64289 = 161289.

items.q: If cos θ = 513 and θ is in the first quadrant, find cos 2θ.
items.e: First, sin θ = 1213 (sign from the first quadrant). cos 2θ = cos² θ − sin² θ = 25169 − 144169 = −119169.

items.q: What is the period of f(x) = sin 5x?
items.e: sin has period 2π, so sin 5x has period 2π ÷ 5 = 2π/5.

items.q: What is the period of f(x) = 3tan 4x?
items.e: tan has period π, so tan 4x has period π ÷ 4 = π/4.

items.q: What is the period of f(x) = cos 4x?
items.e: cos has period 2π, so cos 4x has period 2π ÷ 4 = π/2.

items.q: What is the period of f(x) = cos 5x?

items.q: If cos θ = 513 and θ is in the fourth quadrant, find sin 2θ.
items.e: First, sin θ = −1213 (sign from the fourth quadrant). sin 2θ = 2 sin θ cos θ = 2(−1213)(513) = −120169.

items.q: What is the period of f(x) = 2tan 4x?
items.e: tan has period π, so tan 4x has period π ÷ 4 = π/4.

items.q: If sin θ = −45 and θ is in the third quadrant, find cos 2θ.
items.e: First, cos θ = −35 (sign from the third quadrant). cos 2θ = cos² θ − sin² θ = 925 − 1625 = −725.

items.q: If sin θ = −45 and θ is in the fourth quadrant, find sin 2θ.
items.e: First, cos θ = 35 (sign from the fourth quadrant). sin 2θ = 2 sin θ cos θ = 2(−45)(35) = −2425.

items.q: What is the range of f(x) = 2 sin x − 1?
items.e: sin x lies between −1 and 1, so 2 sin x lies between −2 and 2: the range is [−3, 1].

items.q: If cos θ = −1213 and θ is in the third quadrant, find tan 2θ.
items.e: First, sin θ = −513 (sign from the third quadrant). tan 2θ = sin 2θ / cos 2θ = 120169 ÷ 119169 = 120119.

items.q: If cos θ = 1517 and θ is in the first quadrant, find tan 2θ.
items.e: First, sin θ = 817 (sign from the first quadrant). tan 2θ = sin 2θ / cos 2θ = 240289 ÷ 161289 = 240161.

items.q: If cos θ = 2425 and θ is in the fourth quadrant, find cos 2θ.
items.e: First, sin θ = −725 (sign from the fourth quadrant). cos 2θ = cos² θ − sin² θ = 576625 − 49625 = 527625.

items.q: What is the period of f(x) = 3cos 6x?
items.e: cos has period 2π, so cos 6x has period 2π ÷ 6 = π/3.
